content.intro: Modern PHP offers stronger type declarations and language constructs for making intent explicit. Choose the narrowest useful type and use enums, attributes, and readonly design only when they model a real rule. In this lesson, focus on the object type; then compare it with class and interface types. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use object types and class-related types when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Modern PHP offers stronger type declarations and language constructs for making intent explicit. Choose the narrowest useful type and use enums, attributes, and readonly design only when they model a real rule. For object types and class-related types, begin with the object type. Also distinguish class and interface types; self and parent; static return types. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Object Types and Class-Related Types
content_blocks.code:
<?php
interface Notifier { public function send(string $message): string; }
final class LogNotifier implements Notifier { public function send(string $message): string { return "logged: " . $message; } }
echo (new LogNotifier())->send("ready") . PHP_EOL;
